questions.text: When assessing circulation for a ____________ adult patient you should assess the radial pulse.
The five common vital signs are pulse, respirations, blood pressure, pupils, and ____________.
Respiratory rate can be assessed by watching and feeling the chest and abdomen ____________ during breathing.
Carotid and femoral are the two pulse points that are referred to as ____________ pulses.
Skin that is ____________ in color is called cyanotic.
A respiratory rate that is lower than ____________ for an adult should be considered inadequate.
The term trending is best ____________ as the ability to record changes in a patient's condition over time.
A ____________ has been involved in a rollover vehicle collision, in this scenario, the rollover is an example of the mechanism of injury.
The steps of ____________ assessment include forming a general impression, assessing mental status, assessing ABCs, and determining priority for transport.
A patient who presents with normal vital signs and shows no indications of life threatening problems may be described as ____________.
When assessing a trauma patient who has a significant mechanism of injury, the BP-DOC assessment tool is designed to look for ____________ of traumatic injury.
The secondary assessment is designed to find and treat non-life-threatening ____________.
____________, myocardial infarction, and heart failure are all common causes of cardiac compromise.
____________ is a leading cause of sudden cardiac arrest describes the relationship between a heart attack and sudden cardiac arrest.
You have arrived on the scene of an unresponsive patient whom you find to be pulseless and apneic, you should begin ____________.
